format.description: `csv`: UTF-8 text with a header row, as in RFC 4180; a `json` field is written as JSON text in its cell. `json`: an array of objects, one per record.

content.description: The file as text, at most 10,000,000 characters and as many bytes of UTF-8, and 50,000 rows (`400 validation_error`, rule `too_large` or `too_many_rows`; the latter is raised as soon as the 50,001st row is read, so it does not say how many there are). A byte order mark at the start of a JSON file is ignored.

anyOf.description: A collection key or a field key: `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,62}$`. Keys appear in URLs, filters and record bodies; `label` is the text people read.

additionalProperties.description: The key of the field the column is imported into, the literal `robot`, or an empty string to leave the column out.

mapping.description: Where each column of the file goes, by the column name in the header (for JSON, the property name). A column that is not listed is imported into the field with the same key. A column named after a system field (`id`, `created_at`, `created_by`, `updated_at`, `updated_by`, `revision`, `robot_id`) is left out unless it is mapped.

propertyNames.description: A collection key or a field key: `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,62}$`. Keys appear in URLs, filters and record bodies; `label` is the text people read.

additionalProperties.description: A collection key or a field key: `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,62}$`. Keys appear in URLs, filters and record bodies; `label` is the text people read.

references.description: For each reference field, by its key: the unique field of the target collection that the values in its column identify, for example `name`. A reference field that is not listed takes record ids.

key.description: A unique field that matches rows to existing records: a row whose value is found updates that record, the rest create records. Without a key every row creates a record. A collection with one record per robot is only updated, matched by robot, takes no key and no mirror, and two rows for one robot are an error.

mode.description: `upsert` (the default) creates and updates records. `mirror` also deletes the records of `scope` that are not in the file, and needs `key`. A mirror deletes at most 50,000 records, a file without rows is refused, and a deletion that a `prevent` reference blocks fails the whole import.

filter.description: Only records matching this filter can be deleted. The same filter object that record lists take as JSON text.

robot_id.description: Only records of this robot can be deleted.

scope.description: Limits which records `mirror` may delete: those matching a filter, or those of one robot. Name exactly one of them: an empty `scope` is `400 validation_error` (rule `empty`), and so is a `scope` on an import that is not a `mirror` (rule `needs_mirror`). Without a scope the whole collection is mirrored, every robot's records included. `robot_id` of the request does not narrow a mirror; use `scope.robot_id`.

robot_id.description: The robot every row belongs to, in a collection that belongs to robots, when the file has no `robot` column; sent together with a `robot` column it is refused (rule `robot_column_present`). It says which robot the rows are for and does not narrow a `mirror`: that is `scope.robot_id`.

confirm.description: The `token` of the preview of exactly this import. Without it the import route answers the preview and imports nothing. A token that is not the one of the current preview, because the data moved on or it belongs to another import, is answered `409 confirmation_required` with the current preview in `details.preview`. A file with errors is never imported: its preview comes back with `token: null`, whatever `confirm` says.

description: Imports a file of records into a collection, all or nothing.
